messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Pager: PROD model-serving error spike for route /v1/generate (severity: P2). Affected model: redwood-m-7b-q8@v2.3. Trigger: 5xx rate > 2% over 5m. First observed 03:12:10 UTC.

emily: saw the bot. I'm oncall — pulling logs now. tagging @raj for model-side.

raj: on it. any rough customer impact?

emily: alerting notes: 3 customer-facing apps saw increased 502s, tail latency up. console shows canary traffic is 10% to v2.3 since 02:50 UTC.

sasha: from infra side I'm seeing intermittent OOMs in the canary pod pool (us-west1-gpu-a). kube events: pod evicted + restart loop for canary replicas around 03:06-03:10.

raj: hmm OOM + 5xx could be kv cache/sequence explosion. sharing a snippet of the model logs now.

raj: ```
2026-03-15T03:09:58Z ERROR handler: request_id=rcp-9a2f tokenization failed: InvalidTokenSequenceError
stack: transformer/tokenizer.cc: line 243
2026-03-15T03:10:01Z WARN runtime: kv-cache miss spike: 142x baseline
2026-03-15T03:10:02Z ERROR runtime: out-of-memory allocating attention_kv (size=1.1GB)
```

maria: customer impact: product analytics flagged 18 interrupted sessions (mostly autocomplete) — estimated 0.4% of total active sessions during window. Not huge but visible on dashboards.

emily: timeline so far: 02:50 - canary v2.3 promoted to 10% traffic. 03:06 - infra notices pod restarts. 03:12 - pager fired. 03:18 - oncall triage thread started.

ops-bot: deployment activity detected: canary rollout redwood-m-7b-q8@v2.3 by ci/cd pipeline (change set 8472) — config includes quantize=q8 + custom-kernel-flag.

raj: important detail: v2.3 includes a new tokenizer patch (tokenizer v1.7) and an experimental KV caching rewrite. both touch memory and token processing.

sasha: I can scale down canary traffic with routing policy now if we want to limit impact.

emily: proposed mitigations (ranked): 1) shift canary to 0% traffic (traffic shift) 2) pin route to previous stable model v2.2 for all production routes 3) restart canary nodes with higher mem to test OOM reproduction 4) rollback full rollout. Thoughts? :thinking_face:

raj: quick thinking: pin to v2.2 for prod routes immediately, keep canary pool isolated for debug. v2.3 will remain on dedicated debug nodes. I want to repro using failing request ids.

maria: agree with pin. customers flagged interruptions but no major SLAs breached yet. Recommend pin to reduce fallout. :thumbsup:

emily: executing traffic pin now. will update when complete.

deploy-bot: command received: set-route-model --route "/v1/generate" --model redwood-m-7b-q8@v2.2 --token=ops-token-***
deploy-bot: result: OK. Traffic pinned to v2.2 as of 03:21:05 UTC.

emily: traffic pin completed at 03:21:05 UTC. observed 502s dropping back towards baseline in the next 2 minutes.

sasha: confirming: canary pool still restarting but it's on isolated nodes; no further customer impact after pin. I also captured node metrics (attach link) — CPU stable, memory spikes coincide with tokenization errors.

raj: capturing failing request ids to run local repro. sample request id: rcp-9a2f, rcp-9b3c, rcp-9f7d. saving model artifacts from the canary nodes: /artifacts/canary/8472/trace-20260315.tar.gz

emily: good. I'm going to update the incident summary and notify oncall handoff in 30m if stable.

maria: doc update: logging affected customers list to support.raising a low-priority customer comms item in case we need to proactively notify.

raj: quick hypotheses (ranked):
1) tokenizer v1.7 regression -> InvalidTokenSequenceError under q8 quantization path
2) KV cache rewrite introduced memory leak on certain sequence patterns -> OOMs
3) kernel selection mismatch for new compilation flag causing invalid memory access

sasha: testing hypothesis 2: I ran a local stress with long-seq workload and reproduced kv-cache miss spike and OOM after ~5000 requests. attaching small trace:
```
# reproducer run (shortened)
seq_len=4096, batch=1
kv-cache-miss: baseline=0.8 per-s, repro=120 per-s
OOM at iter 512: alloc failure attention_kv size=1.1GB
```

raj: testing hypothesis 1: tokenizer unit tests pass but integration shows token boundary handling diverges for rare unicode sequences. I'll run repro with the recorded request payloads.

emily: decision log: immediate mitigation done = traffic pin to v2.2 (03:21:05). Next actions: (A) collect full crash dumps from canary nodes and upload to S3, (B) run local repro for tokenizer + kv scenarios, (C) decide rollback vs patch after repro.

ops-bot: artifact upload complete: s3://redwood-incidents/2876543210/canary-artifacts/ (files: trace-20260315.tar.gz, memdump-03-10.gz, node-metrics.json)

raj: running repro now; will post results in ~20m. can someone add the change set + PR link for v2.3?

emily: PR here: https://git.redwood.ai/infra/modeling/merge_requests/1274 (changes: tokenizer v1.7 bump, kv-rewrite, compile-flag experimental).

maria: devex note: we should add a quick checklist for customer templating if we need to send a post-incident note.

sasha: ops follow-up: I recommend we don't roll back the entire cluster yet — pinning minimized user impact. full rollback if repro shows critical corruption.

raj: repro update: tokenizer repro shows failure for payload with mixed ZWJ sequences and surrogate pair near boundary, which triggers invalid split with tokenizer v1.7 when using the quantized tokenizer table. kv-repro also shows memory growth but slower on local debug builds.

emily: interim verdict: primary hypothesis = tokenizer + q8 path interaction causing tokenization exceptions that cascade to runtime memory churn. secondary hypothesis = kv-cache memory handling exacerbates OOMs.

maria: agreed. Plan for RCA:
- postmortem owners: raj (model), sasha (infra), emily (incident lead), maria (customer comms)
- collect timeline + logs + reproducible test cases (artifacts already uploaded)
- PR revert vs patch options: fast patch to tokenizer table OR rollback ci change to keep tokenizer v1.6 for q8 path

emily: I'm assigning the handoff: @raj owning model repro + fix PR, @sasha owning infra replay and node-proofing, @maria owning comms draft. We will reconvene in #incidents in 2 hours or earlier if new findings.

incident-bot: Incident P2 transitioned to Monitoring (no active pager) at 03:40:12 UTC. Root thread archived for RCA coordination.

emily: thanks team. uploading interim incident notes to the incident tracker. I'll leave the thread open for a few hours for RCA updates.

raj: quick note — if we decide rollback: simple command is deploy rollback redwood-m-7b-q8 --to v2.2 --scope all. Prefer pin+patch to full cluster rollback if possible.

sasha: added checklist to infra runbook for next steps (increase mem limit on canary nodes, run long-seq load tests, validate tokenizers on quantized path).

maria: will draft customer note and share for review.

emily: closing loop: incident mitigated, customer impact low but visible; RCA owners assigned; artifacts collected; next update in two hours or on new findings. :white_check_mark:
